title: dynamic-slot-packer-and-sustained-minimum-allocator-for-fragmentation-reduction
author: Priya Sharma
release_notes:
- Introduces Dynamic Slot Packer to reduce slot fragmentation and increase utilization across dedicated fleets.
- Adds Sustained Minimum Allocator to guarantee a low throughput floor for critical tenant classes.
- New telemetry: slot_fragmentation_ratio, packing_efficiency_ratio, sustained_min_alloc_success_rate.
- No API changes to public inference surface; internal allocator behavior only.
description:
Motivation and summary:
Transient demand patterns for a subset of tenants were causing high slot fragmentation in Dedicated fleets: many slots partially used by low-concurrency tenants, which increased cost and reduced available capacity for large requests. This PR adds two complementary mechanisms: (1) Dynamic Slot Packer — a scheduler-side heuristic that packs compatible low-concurrency allocations into underutilized GPU slots in soft-isolated 'micro-slices' to reclaim capacity; and (2) Sustained Minimum Allocator — a safety allocator that enforces a lightweight minimum throughput floor for tenants flagged as critical, preventing starvation during aggressive downscales.

What this PR does (high level):
- Runtime: implement dynamic slot packing logic in the dedicated allocator with conservative compatibility checks (model occlusion, seq_len bucket, quantization footprint) and eviction hooks.
- Policy: introduce tenant annotation for sustained-minimum class and a configurable per-tenant min-throughput target expressed as ops/sec.
- Telemetry: emit slot_fragmentation_ratio, packing_efficiency_ratio, slot_packing_rebalances, and sustained_min_alloc_success_rate to the telemetry pipeline.
- Tests: unit tests for packer compatibility, integration test simulating 200 tenants with mixed concurrencies, and e2e scenario that verifies no regression on latency SLOs for high-priority tenants.
- Docs: operator guide with knobs (packing_threshold, slice_size_hint, sustained_min_backoff) and examples for safe rollout.

Review thread (high-level):
- Noah Patel (review): "Nice direction — packing seems promising, but need to be careful about KV cache isolation and tail-latency regressions. Please add a safety timeout after which a packed slice is drained before eviction to avoid long-tail interferences."
- Author (Priya): "Added a new 'slice_drain_timeout' config and drained-pack eviction in commit 3. Also added integration checks to ensure no SVR tail increase > 5th percentile baseline."
- Maya Chen (review): "Can we avoid cross-tenant GPU kernel contention for certain quantized kernels? Suggest making kernel-family a compatibility dimension."
- Author (Priya): "Updated compatibility predicate to include kernel family and added a unit test for quantized-kernel mismatch."
- Diego Alvarez (approval): "Benchmarks look good; packing increased usable capacity by ~13% in our synthetic mix without SLO regressions. Approved pending CI green."

CI and validation:
- First run: dedicated-mixed-tenants job failed (integration: timeout in teardown). Rerun after fix to test harness in commit 4.
- Second run: all unit tests passed, integration scenario completed, regression check passed, lint + build passed. CI status: pass.
- Performance lab: measured 12.8% reduction in effective slot count (i.e., reclaimed capacity) and tail latency increase <1ms for 99th percentile on critical tenants.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Packing is off by default. Default operator chart sets packing_threshold=0.0. Canary rollout steps documented: enable packing in 1% of fleet via release gates, monitor packing_efficiency_ratio and slot_fragmentation_ratio, increase to 10% then 50% if stable.
- Sustained Minimum Allocator is opt-in per-tenant and has a graceful backoff to avoid starving best-effort traffic.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New metrics added: slot_fragmentation_ratio (gauge), packing_efficiency_ratio (gauge), slot_packing_rebalances (counter), sustained_min_alloc_success_rate (ratio)
- Added dashboard: Dedicated -> Capacity -> Packing Efficiency with heatmap by pool and tenant class.

Migration notes:
- No external API changes. Operator must add new chart values to enable packer and tune slice_size_hint. Operators upgrading chart without changes will see no behavior change.

If there's any concern about the eviction semantics or additional safety gates, I can split the packer into a separate feature flag and roll the minimum allocator independently in a follow-up.
